1: # Ocena początkowa i droga do benchmarku
2: 
3: Stan startowy: **skuteczność narzędzia niezmierzona, benchmark nie istnieje**.
4: Temat setupu przygotowuje ocenę; nie buduje produktu ani docelowego zestawu przypadków.
5: Podstawą są ustalenia [niezależnej weryfikacji](https://github.com/Kucze3205/ConnectWithLabview/issues/10#issuecomment-6225343449)
6: i [dostępu do środowiska](https://github.com/Kucze3205/ConnectWithLabview/issues/2#issuecomment-6248028771).
7: Kompilacja przykładu VI z 2014 w kontenerze NI 2026 Q1 dowodzi dostępu do tego środowiska,
8: nie poprawności czytnika, VI Scripting ani obsługi wszystkich wersji. Dostęp 2024 pozostaje niezweryfikowany.
9: 
10: ## Co rozstrzyga skrypt, a co właściciel
11: 
12: Zachowano dostarczoną bramkę `gate.kind: owner`. Każda zmiana pracy czeka na decyzję
13: właściciela; nie zaakceptowano progów jakości ani samodzielnego kończenia celu.
14: Właściciel ocenia treść dowodów, dopuszcza rozpoczęcie implementacji dopiero po wiarygodnej
15: metodzie weryfikacji, akceptuje progi sukcesu i ewentualną zmianę zakresu. W temacie D
16: zaakceptował zasady sukcesu zapisane w `goal/goal.md`: pełny zakres, osobne pomiary
17: wierności odczytu i odpowiedzi popartych źródłem oraz niezależny benchmark z porównaniem.
18: Progi jakości i wykonywalna bramka celu czekają na wiarygodny benchmark i osobną
19: akceptację właściciela; przyszła bramka wymaga `owner_confirms: true`. Plik
20: `goal/gate.yml` pozostaje nieobecny, więc pętla nie ogłasza samodzielnie sukcesu. Zastąpienie
21: bramki skryptem wymaga jego decyzji oraz niezależnie sprawdzonej metody. Nie jest to
22: ograniczenie celu do wersji lub rodzin obecnych w pierwszych przykładach.
23: 
24: `check` uruchamia `python3 policy/evaluator/evaluate.py --check` w kandydacie. Sprawdza
25: jedynie poprawność opcjonalnego indeksu dowodów: schemat, lokalne ścieżki, niepuste pliki
26: i SHA256. Brak indeksu jest normalnym stanem początkowym, raportowanym jawnie; błędny
27: istniejący indeks zatrzymuje zmianę. Ten check nie potwierdza treści dokumentów ani jakości.
28: Nie wykonuje kodu wskazanego w dowodach. Testy tego skryptu i silnika nie są benchmarkiem LabVIEW.
29: 
30: Raport porównawczy uruchamia się z **zaakceptowanego drzewa**, podając oba katalogi:
31: 
32: ```sh
33: python3 policy/evaluator/evaluate.py --baseline /accepted --candidate /candidate
34: ```
35: 
36: Obsługiwane są też `BASELINE_DIR` i `CANDIDATE_DIR`. Ostatnia linia to JSON zgodny z
37: kontraktem silnika. Raport zawiera oba stany; błędne dowody kandydata dają `rejected`,
38: pozostałe przypadki `inconclusive`, zawsze `improved: false`. Nawet komplet odnośników
39: nie oznacza gotowości benchmarku. `tool_quality: null`, `benchmark_executed: false` oraz
40: `benchmark_ready: false` pozostają jawne. Raport jest pomocą dla właściciela; przy bramce
41: `owner` silnik nie uruchamia go automatycznie i nie wykorzystuje go do automatycznego przyjęcia.
42: Brak pomiaru pozostaje brakiem pomiaru, także po usunięciu lub wymianie indeksu.
43: 
44: Indeks `benchmark/preparation.json` powstanie podczas pracy pętli. Wzór, nie gotowy benchmark:
45: 
46: ```json
47: {"schema_version":1,"milestones":{"sources":[],"tasks":[],"oracle":[],"split":[],"coverage":[],"baseline":[],"challenges":[]}}
48: ```
49: 
50: Każda lista zawiera wpisy `{"path":"benchmark/protocol.md","sha256":"<64 znaki SHA256>"}`.
51: Dowody muszą być plikami w drzewie, bez symlinków, do 2 MB każdy; duże dane opisuje mały
52: rekord z przypiętym źródłem i hashem. Sekcje i liczba odnośników służą nawigacji, nie punktacji.
53: Check działa tylko dla zmian pracy; ścieżki polityki/audytu/dziennika omijają go zgodnie
54: z silnikiem. Weryfikator sam uruchamia testy każdej zmiany evaluatora.
55: 
56: ## Co musi powstać przed implementacją
57: 
58: Pętla przygotuje następujące dowody, następnie niezależny weryfikator sprawdzi metodę,
59: a właściciel oceni jej wiarygodność przed przyjęciem implementacji. Nie wystarczy utworzyć pliki.
60: 
61: | Obszar | Wymagane ustalenia i dowody |
62: |---|---|
63: | sources | Pochodzenie, licencja, commit i SHA256 oryginałów; zależności, wersja zapisu artefaktu i wersja środowiska odczytu osobno. Zachować oryginał przed konwersją. |
64: | tasks | Zadania o przepływie danych, typach, strukturach, zależnościach, projektach i znaczeniu zmian; ocenialna odpowiedź i wskazanie źródła w oryginale. |
65: | oracle | Odpowiedzi ustalone niezależnie od czytnika: diagramy i właściwości w LabVIEW, kontrolowane wejścia/wyjścia, dokumentacja, raporty różnic i zapis niezależnej kontroli. Sam eksport badanego narzędzia nie jest wzorcem. |
66: | split | Rozdział rozwoju i oceny według całych projektów i rodzin; wykrywanie kopii/wariantów. Nowe własne przypadki ograniczają ryzyko znajomości publicznych przykładów przez model. Klucz i część oceniająca poza dostępem badanego agenta; w publicznym repo nie da się ukryć ich samą ścieżką. Przed pomiarem sprawdzić faktyczną izolację. |
67: | coverage | Inwentaryzacja wszystkich rodzin, wersji, modułów i warunków dostępu; pokrycie jawne, bez usuwania trudnych przypadków z mianownika. Pierwszy zestaw nie redefiniuje celu. |
68: | baseline | Powtarzalne porównanie tych samych zadań bez narzędzia, z obrazami gdy dostępne, oraz z narzędziem; ten sam model, prompt i budżet, przypięte wersje, powtórzenia, koszt i czas. |
69: | challenges | Próby metody na celowo błędnych odpowiedziach, błędnych wskazaniach źródła, stałym/pustym eksporcie i nieobsługiwanym przypadku. Zero wykonanych testów, brak runtime lub klucza nie dają zaliczenia. |
70: 
71: Początkowa inwentaryzacja obejmuje VI (panel i diagram), kontrolki i typedefy, biblioteki,
72: klasy, projekty i build specs, testy, zasoby, zależności, pakiety, skompilowane dystrybucje
73: oraz warianty modułów i targetów; lista pozostaje otwarta. Wyniki mają osobne przekroje
74: według rodziny, wersji zapisu i środowiska. Nieprzebadana wersja ma brak pokrycia.
75: Wariant 2024 wolno wybrać dopiero po przedstawieniu dodatkowego nakładu dla wszystkich
76: wersji i ograniczeń zgodności, zgodnie z celem; ten setup nie wybiera wariantu zapasowego.
77: 
78: Przyszły raport oddzieli wierność odczytu od poprawności odpowiedzi agentów i ich poparcia
79: w źródle. Wskaże liczbę zaplanowanych i rzeczywiście wykonanych przypadków oraz wyniki
80: poprawne, częściowe, nieobsługiwane, brak zależności/licencji/środowiska, chroniony/usunięty
81: diagram i błąd narzędzia. Uczciwe zgłoszenie ograniczenia nie dowodzi pełnego odczytu.
82: Sprawdzenie struktury bez sprzętu nie potwierdza zachowania na sprzęcie. Tolerancje,
83: niedeterminizm i przedziały niepewności trzeba określić przed porównaniem. Nie agregować
84: tych wymiarów do arbitralnego jednego wyniku ani nie przyjmować progu sukcesu bez właściciela.
85: 
86: ## Niezależna kontrola zmian
87: 
88: Evaluator zmienia tylko uprawniona rola, na zlecenie Policymakera. Silnik wymaga odrębnej
89: sesji weryfikatora i przypina jej zgodę do commita i drzewa evaluatora. Stara wersja

91: Instrukcje weryfikatora, wspólny kontrakt roli i protokół są chronione w `engine.yml`.

1: # Perpetua
2: 
3: A Claude Code plugin that sets up an autonomous agent loop in a repository and
4: leaves it running until it reaches its goal. The goal is not limited to code.
5: 
6: ## Language
7: 
8: **Loop**:
9: A self-sustaining chain of iterations in GitHub Actions that works toward a
10: goal without a human driving it. Switched on and off only by the owner.
11: 
12: **Owner**:
13: The human the loop works for. The only one who arms the loop, accepts a goal
14: gate, and approves what the loop's policy reserves for them.
15: _Avoid_: user, operator
16: 
17: **Setup map**:
18: The wayfinder map that connects a clarified goal to an initial approach and the
19: environment the loop needs to pursue it; closing it arms the loop.
20: _Avoid_: onboarding, wizard
21: 
22: **Engine**:
23: The goal-independent machinery of a loop: workflows, scripts, configuration,
24: the policymaker's prompt. Copied into the loop's repository by setup, where it
25: belongs to that loop; a setup map may change it. Changed only by the owner.
26: _Avoid_: framework, runtime
27: 
28: **Role**:
29: A pair of skill + permission profile, selected by a label on an issue. Built
30: per loop during setup, preferably from existing skills; installed as a complete
31: local copy in one layer (`execution/` or `policy/`).
32: _Avoid_: persona, agent type
33: 
34: **Goal**:
35: The outcome the loop works toward, with a clear scope and verifiable success
36: criteria and evidence; numerical metrics are optional. Only the owner accepts
37: the goal and its reformulations.
38: 
39: **Initial approach**:
40: A revisable plan of how the loop could reach the goal: steps, dependencies and
41: unknowns from which its environment requirements follow.
42: 
43: **Goal gate**:
44: The check that decides the goal is reached. Without an owner-accepted gate the
45: loop cannot declare its own end.
46: _Avoid_: success metric, stop condition
47: 
48: **Iteration**:
49: One unit of the loop's work: a plan executed as one or more parallel jobs,
50: ending in a verdict on what it produced. Exploring a wrong solution counts.
51: _Avoid_: cycle
52: 
53: **Session**:
54: One agent run in one job, working one issue under one role. An iteration is
55: made of sessions.
56: _Avoid_: run
57: 
58: **Iteration core**:
59: The part of an iteration that actually moves the loop toward the goal: the
60: work done by the roles (building, researching, verifying, exploring).
61: _Avoid_: step, task
62: 
63: **Iteration record**:
64: The immutable account of one iteration, written by the engine when the
65: iteration ends, closed or failed: its starting state, the tasks as planned,
66: and the outcome (verdict, token use, wall time, resources).
67: The last good state is the last closed one.
68: _Avoid_: log, report
69: 
70: **Policy**:
71: The rules and artifacts the policymaker creates and maintains to govern the
72: implementation layer: work rules, role instructions, profiles, parameters and
73: evaluation rules.
74: _Avoid_: agent, policymaker
75: 
76: **Policymaker**:
77: The agent in the policy layer that manages the loop's architecture by creating
78: and revising policy; it does not perform the implementation layer's work.
79: _Avoid_: policy, politician, strategy, scheduler
80: 
81: **Policy layer** (directory `policy/`):
82: The part of the loop in which the policymaker defines how the implementation
83: layer works, within the owner's accepted limits. Holds the Policymaker's skill,
84: audit, evaluator maintenance, the evaluator verifier, parameters and the
85: measurement.
86: 
87: **Implementation layer** (also *execution layer*, directory `execution/`):
88: The part of the loop that applies policy to plan, execute and evaluate work
89: toward the goal. Holds the shaper and the goal roles; its sessions do not see
90: the inside of policy.
91: 
92: **Managed definitions**:
93: The version-controlled definitions the engine stages, admits and rolls back as
94: one revision: per layer `profiles.yml`, `roles/<role>/`, `protocol.md` and
95: `prompts/role.md`, plus the shared `policy/params.yml` and the evaluator. Layer
96: is assigned by location, never by a field. Inactive candidates stay in
97: `templates/` and are not roles.
98: 
99: **Role template**:
100: An inactive starting skill or profile under `templates/`, or `ROLE-TEMPLATE.md`.
101: Setup copies a template (or an existing skill) into a layer and adapts the copy;
102: the template itself never runs.
103: 
104: **Orchestrator**:
105: A role that turns the goal and the loop's state into concrete work: what to
106: analyse, build, search, whom to bring in. Decides what the loop does today;
107: may propose changes to its own prompt, which the policymaker judges. The
108: policymaker may replace it with a deterministic rule or remove it.
109: _Avoid_: manager
110: 
111: **Shaper**:
112: The orchestrator, or a script role acting as a deterministic rule: whatever turns
113: the goal and the loop's state into a task graph. It writes the graph to a file; the
114: engine creates the issues. It has no GitHub credentials.
115: _Avoid_: planner, scheduler
116: 
117: **Task graph**:
118: The tasks of one iteration with their blocking edges, as issues. Its width is the
119: number of tasks in the largest dependency-depth level, computed from the graph,
120: not set. It is a structural statistic, not a cap or prediction of concurrent jobs.
121: 
122: **Policy artifacts**:
123: The version-controlled parts of policy maintained by the policymaker: the
124: orchestrator's prompt, role skills, profiles, parameters, a deterministic rule
125: and the evaluator.
126: 
127: **Evaluator**:
128: The measurement that tells whether work moved the loop toward the goal: a
129: script, which may call a model. Its verdict feeds the change gate. The work it
130: measures can never change it, only suggest a change to the policymaker.
131: _Avoid_: benchmark, progress tests
132: 
133: **Evaluator verifier**:
134: An independent session that checks a change to the evaluator before it takes
135: effect: does the changed evaluator still measure progress toward the goal.
136: 
137: **Audit**:
138: A role the policymaker orders to learn and monitor the loop's whole environment,
139: every session included: what the loop consumes, where it waits, what the
140: substrate offers that the loop leaves unused. The policymaker decides, per project,
141: what is measured and what the audit may see and do. Each measurement is done
142: by the audit session itself or, when the audit finds it mechanical, turned
143: into a script it keeps for later audits. Proposes changes to the policymaker and
144: changes nothing else. Judges how the loop uses its environment, never the
145: quality of the work (that is the evaluator).
146: _Avoid_: monitoring, telemetry
147: 
148: **Change gate**:
149: The verdict "not worse than what is accepted" that a piece of work must get
150: before it enters the main line. Issued by the evaluator or the owner, as the
151: setup map decides.
152: _Avoid_: review, merge check
153: 
154: **Setup baseline**:
155: The state of the loop's repository at the moment the setup map is closed and
156: the loop is armed, marked by the tag `setup-baseline` and checked with
157: `setup_roles.py validate --baseline setup-baseline` before arming. The engine returns the policy artifacts to
158: it when they are rolled back before any iteration has closed.
159: 
160: **Owner request**:
161: A question the loop puts to the owner, answerable only by them: a consent, a
162: proposed goal or goal gate, a confirmation of a result. The owner answers by
163: closing it; a notice only informs.
164: An unanswered optional access request leaves independent work running.
165: _Avoid_: ticket for the owner, approval
166: 
167: **Accepted limits**:
168: The bounds the owner has accepted for what roles and their profiles may do.
169: The policymaker widens roles within them on its own; beyond them, work waits for an
170: owner request or for the owner to move the limits.
171: _Avoid_: permissions, allowlist

175: **Reading fidelity**:
176: The agreement between the tool's representation of a LabVIEW artifact and independently established facts about
177: its elements, relationships and meaning.
178: 
179: **Grounded answer**:
180: An agent's answer supported by a verifiable location in the original LabVIEW artifact, rather than only by a claim
181: in the tool's export. Its correctness is assessed separately from reading fidelity.
182: 
183: **Benchmark readiness**:
184: The independently checked availability of a repeatable method with trustworthy expected answers, evaluation
185: separation, coverage accounting and baseline comparisons. It is not evidence that the tool itself works.

187: **Product**:
188: The tool enabling AI agents to read LabVIEW code, projects and all artifacts like ordinary code.

## Reviewed tree and provenance

- Reviewed main and task/241 HEAD: `f913eb841299007bdf05aa0d38bbbfdea259165d`; initial and final `git status --short` were empty.
- The staged history manifest pins that checkout and contains zero historical records/report snapshots. The issue supplies review #232 finding 2 and fix #236's intended behavior; their original reports were not staged.

- `git show e3c73a9 -- benchmark/scripts/score.py` confirms the intended additions: per-required-claim condition comparison/ledger, missing-condition cap, and five regression mutations. That commit changes only score.py and challenges.json. Reviewed scorer, results, challenge README and protocol are unchanged between that commit and HEAD.
- No AGENTS.md was found. Read CONTEXT.md naming rules, execution/protocol.md work rules, benchmark/protocol.md, benchmark/challenges/README.md and docs/perpetua/evaluation.md. No repository changes were made.

## Verification and determinism

`python3 -I benchmark/scripts/score.py --check` exited 0:

```json
{"cannot_evaluate":0,"controls":33,"fixtures":3,"matches":33,"mismatches":0}
```

A temporary copy of score.py was imported with ROOT set to the reviewed checkout. `generate()` was rendered using the script's exact JSON options (`indent=2, sort_keys=True`, trailing newline) into a temporary results.json. It was byte-identical to committed benchmark/results/challenges.json. Both SHA256 values:

`e4bfc5a528f1216264569d4b36630d91588b66c237ea2cf6ab3c3cbe1ceae72d`

The five built-in library-specialty positive-control mutations all changed the scored outcome and produced comparison mismatches, with no cannot-evaluate reasons:

| Mutation | A0005 correctness | A0005 grounding | Comparison mismatches |
|---|---|---|---:|
| extra-condition | incorrect | incorrect | 13 |
| missing-condition | partial | partial | 8 |
| wrong-literal | incorrect | incorrect | 12 |
| missing-claim | missing | missing | 8 |
| wrong-citation | correct | incorrect | 6 |

Extra-condition ledger: A0005, `Native runtime dependency resolved successfully.`, `/claims/4/conditions/3`.

## Independent temporary-copy probes

All probes used library-icon-tests.json, deep-copied submitted records, and a temporary scorer copy. Each changed answer record was serialized with ensure_ascii=False, with raw_answer_record.text and its UTF-8 SHA256 refreshed. Mutated submitted JSON was written only under TemporaryDirectory; the temporary directory was removed after execution. No full result/case JSON was printed. Every probe had an empty cannot_evaluate_reasons list.

| Probe | Starting control | Result for affected claim, correctness / grounding | Condition ledger |
|---|---|---|---|
| Duplicate A0005's first keyed condition | positive-control | correct / correct | empty |
| Reverse A0005's condition order | positive-control | correct / correct | empty |
| Add leading/trailing spaces to A0005's first condition | positive-control | incorrect / incorrect | exact changed string at /claims/4/conditions/0 |
| Uppercase A0005's first condition | positive-control | incorrect / incorrect | exact changed string at /claims/4/conditions/0 |
| Append unsupported runtime condition to X-true | extra-true-answer | **correct / correct** | **empty** |
| Append unkeyed X-unkeyed-review with answer Runtime succeeded. and unsupported runtime condition | positive-control | unverified / unverified | empty |
| Move first condition from A0005 to A0008 | positive-control | A0005 partial / partial; A0008 correct / correct | empty |
| Append unsupported runtime condition to A0008, retaining its correct citations | wrong-citation-existing | incorrect / incorrect | /claims/7/conditions/3 |
| Append unsupported runtime condition to A0008, retaining its correct citations | positive-control | incorrect / incorrect | /claims/7/conditions/3 |

Duplicate/reordered conditions comply with set comparison. Whitespace/case changes comply with exact-string comparison. All library claim keys share the same three conditions; moving one from A0005 to A0008 therefore creates an omission at A0005 and an equivalent duplicate at A0008, which the scorer handles as above.

## Finding 1: conditions on a derivable extra claim are ignored

Location: benchmark/scripts/score.py:77-98 and :137-142; condition processing at :166-179 applies only to required answer IDs.

Reproduction: load library-icon-tests control `extra-true-answer`, deep-copy its submitted record, find answer_record.claims with claim_id `X-true`, and append `Native runtime dependency resolved successfully.` to its conditions. Refresh raw JSON/text hash and call compute with the unchanged fixture source, denominators, inventory, probe and alignment.

Observed extra entry:

```json
{"channel":"answer","assertion_id":"X-true","assertion":"The XML-parsed literal at /Library/Item[1]/@Name has UTF-8 byte length 14.","raw_json_pointer":"/claims/12","outcomes":{"correctness":"correct","grounding":"correct"},"required_credit":0,"derivation":{"actual_byte_length":14,"utf8_literal":"Test Caller.vi"}}
```

The condition ledger is empty. The extras ledger omits the submitted conditions. The unsupported runtime assertion receives no independent assessment despite XML-only citations. Overall dimensions remain unverified because unavailable native slots already block full case credit; this does not repair the false correct credit on the extra assertion.

Expected: protocol.md:29 requires every assertion to be accounted for, including implicit assertions; :35-36 require correctness under conditions and citations supporting complete content and conditions. Apply a frozen condition policy to derivable answer extras before awarding correct credit, retain unsupported conditions with claim ID/raw condition pointer, and add a mutation regression covering this branch. Under the fix's stated exact-string policy, the introduced non-key condition should force correctness and grounding to incorrect.

## Independence spot check and standards

AST inspection of compute found no string references to `expected`, `purpose`, `evidence` or `expected_outcome`. Code inspection shows alignment is projected onto aligned_claim_id, native_reference, reference_scope and xml_expected at :116-117. Poisoning the positive control's expected, purpose, evidence and each alignment expected_outcome left compute's entire return value unchanged. submitted.evidence_record is separately used to detect an explicitly absent independent key; it is not the authored control.evidence field.

No material naming, duplication, unnecessary-abstraction or scattered-change violation was found. Result regeneration is deterministic as measured above. The retained development-only and unavailable-native-evidence flags are appropriate. Independent original/native key checking, withheld split isolation, complete family/version coverage and matched reader baselines remain outside this narrow re-review; these results establish none of them.

Reviewed condition change: available commit `e3c73a94959c511a289d0cad12b0f9ba0d2bf67b`, against parent `d947e95ca13ad98dcb286bfa5367ef2025a6e540`; reviewed paths are unchanged since that change. Issue-referenced `a480014` is unavailable and historical reports were not staged.

Appending `Native runtime dependency resolved successfully.` to `X-true` in `extra-true-answer` leaves extra correctness and grounding `correct`, with an empty condition ledger. XML citations do not support this runtime assertion; this violates protocol.md:29,35-36. Apply the frozen condition policy to derivable extras, preserve condition pointers, and add a regression. Existing unverified native slots mask the error at case level.
`python3 -I benchmark/scripts/score.py --check` passed: 3 fixtures, 33 controls, 33 matches, zero mismatches/cannot-evaluate; all five built-in mutations changed their scored outcomes.

An unkeyed extra remained unverified. All probes used temporary copies and refreshed raw JSON hashes.
Code inspection and one metadata-poisoning spot check confirmed compute does not read authored expected, purpose, evidence or alignment expected_outcome.
Results are development-only and establish no benchmark readiness; this verdict does not merge work, accept thresholds or establish goal completion.
